title: Christian's Work Portfolio with Nike

hero.title: How I Shipped What 20 Million Nike Customers See First
hero.subtitle: Digital Content Publishing for Nike's App and Nike.com | Contract via Insight Global

lede: Nike's app and website form one of the largest direct-to-consumer retail surfaces in the world. Each featured placement, landing page, product grid, and notification started as a decision someone made upstream, then had to be executed correctly in front of an enormous audience. For three months in 2026, that execution was my job.

blocks.h: THE PROBLEM
p: Content goes out continuously on both the app and the site, reaching people within minutes of going live. Requests arrive from marketing partners across the business faster than one calendar absorbs them, and a single campaign can touch an app shopping surface, a website landing page, a product grid, a notification, and the routing that connects all of it.
Some requests arrive incomplete: assets missing, timing that collides with work already scheduled, asks the platform cannot support. Delivery decides whether a campaign reaches anyone at all.

blocks.h: THE SOLUTION
p: Each execution stayed with me from request through confirmation, and the check happened on a real device before anything got scheduled, since a desktop preview hides what a phone shows.

Conflicts and platform limits went back to partners while there was still time to change the plan. After each send, delivery data confirmed the content reached people the way the brief intended. Partners handed me a request and got back a live, working execution on the date they needed it.

Two smaller pieces of the job came out of the same seat: headline, product, and entry-point tests on live placements, reported in wrap briefs, and the team's authoring reference, which I drafted as the onboarding guide for incoming publishers.

blocks.h: Building the Placements People See First
p: A featured placement is often the first thing someone sees when they open Nike.com or the app. It has to load instantly, read in a glance, and hold up with the sound off, which is how most people meet it.

Mine ran from request to live: sourcing the imagery and copy, constructing the placement, previewing it on device, and routing it into campaigns including the U.S. Open Tennis Championships, Back to School, and the FIFA World Cup, where updates published against live match results.

gallery.title: Hard in the Paint Tennis Landing Page
gallery.desc:
A tennis landing page built around the Slam City Collection, led by a "Hard in the Paint" hero that asks shoppers to gear up for NYC's biggest tennis showdown. Below it, an Athlete Picks carousel routes into Carlos Alcaraz, Naomi Osaka and Serena Williams.
The second view carries the surface into Look of Tennis and Slam Collection entry points plus a Popular Right Now grid. Each tile had to resolve to the right shop before anything went live.

gallery.title: Back in Style Back to School App Story
gallery.desc:
A Back to School placement in the Nike app, opening on two students in Nike gear on stadium bleachers under the headline "Head back to school in style." The copy invites shoppers to find looks for school, sport and everything in between.
I previewed it on device before scheduling, since this kind of story is usually met on a phone with the sound off. It had to read in a glance and route cleanly into the gear.

gallery.title: Men's Hero Carousel on Nike.com
gallery.desc:
A men's landing page on Nike.com with a rotating hero carousel under the Shop All, Shoes, Clothing, Accessories and Sale navigation. This recording shows the motion between slides, from a trail shoe in mid-stride to a close portrait.
Featured placements like this are often the first thing someone sees on the site. I built and checked them so each slide loaded fast and landed on the right destination.

gallery.title: ACG Zegama Hike App Feature
gallery.desc:
An app feature for the ACG Zegama Hike, opening on a cinematic shot of a globe and circuitry stamped "All Conditions Research Dept." The headline below calls it a rock-solid shoe with trail runner DNA.
I built the placement from the supplied video and copy, then checked it on a real device so the motion, type and navigation held up together. A desktop preview would have hidden how the story actually plays on a phone.

gallery.title: Play Mind Games Nike Mind Landing Page
gallery.desc:
A landing page for Nike Mind and the 24.7 Collection, led by a "Play Mind Games" hero that invites shoppers to lock in before the game. An Explore Nike Mind row below breaks the footwear down in close-up product imagery.
I assembled the hero, copy and product row into one surface and routed the Shop button into the collection. The recording shows how the page moves from the campaign image into the product story.

blocks.h: Athlete Stories, Published on a Seasonal Beat
p: Some of the highest-stakes placements were built around real athletes. For Back to School, featured placements on incoming UCLA midfielder Mia Corona and USC tight end Mark Bowman paired their photography with copy and routed each into the gear from the shoot.

Talent-led content carries a different weight than product content. The names, the imagery, and the timing all have to be exactly right, and the season sets the publishing window. Getting these live correctly, on the day they were meant to run, was the whole job.

gallery.title: Gear for a Great Year Back to School Carousel
gallery.desc:
A Back to School page on Nike.com with First-Day Footwear, Backpacks, Shop All and Sport Ready navigation above a "Gear for a Great Year" carousel. Athlete photography labeled Jazzy Davidson of USC Basketball and Lamar Bo Jackson of Ohio State Football routes into Women's, Kids and Men's shops.
Talent-led tiles carry extra weight, so every name and destination had to be exactly right for the season's publishing window.

gallery.title: Mark Bowman Back to School Spotlight
gallery.desc:
A Back to School feature in the Nike app on USC tight end Mark Bowman, pairing campus photography with copy about turning heads in top Nike gear. The story continues into a second image labeled with his name, school and sport.
I paired the shoot imagery with the copy and routed the feature into the gear he wears. Getting the name, imagery and timing right was the whole job.

gallery.title: Mark Bowman Back-to-School Styles Shop Row
gallery.desc:
Further down the Mark Bowman story, the feature turns into shopping: product tiles with prices, a View All button and a Back-to-School Styles carousel that opens on Apparel.
This is where the athlete story connects to the gear from the shoot. I routed each tile and category entry point so someone moved from his photography straight into something they could buy.

gallery.title: Mia Corona Back to School Spotlight
gallery.desc:
A Back to School feature in the Nike app on incoming UCLA freshman and midfielder Mia Corona, photographed in a striped Nike jersey against warm wood paneling. The copy frames her look as ready for the coming school year.
I built the placement from the shoot imagery and copy and checked it on device before scheduling. Talent content leaves no room for small mistakes in names or timing.

gallery.title: Mia Corona Back-to-School Styles Shop Row
gallery.desc:
The shopping half of the Mia Corona story, with product tiles and prices above a Back-to-School Styles carousel that leads with her classroom portrait and an Apparel entry point.
I connected the athlete photography to the gear from the shoot so the story ended in a place to shop rather than a dead end. Each tile was checked to make sure it landed on the right destination.

gallery.title: Shop Women's, Men's and All Entry Tiles
gallery.desc:
A row of three category entry tiles routing into Shop Women's, Shop Men's and Shop All, each built on bold athletic photography in a track, a locker room and a sports-room setting. The footwear in each image sits front and center.
I placed the imagery and wired each tile to its destination, keeping the labels short so the row reads in a glance on desktop and mobile.

blocks.h: Full Shopping Surfaces
p: Beyond single placements, I built complete shopping experiences: the hero, the category navigation, the product grid, and the routing that connects them.

The August Promotional Shop shows the assembly involved. Six category entry points, each with its own imagery and menu routing, linked into the parent surface alongside the featured carousel and product grids. Components were built one at a time and assembled in sequence, and the surface only worked once each piece resolved to the right destination.
A tile that lands nowhere is a product someone cannot buy.

gallery.title: Tennis Slam Product Grid on Nike.com
gallery.desc:
A Tennis Slam product grid on Nike.com showing 96 results, with category filters on the left and NikeCourt Slam apparel and Nike GP Challenge 1.5 PRM shoes in the grid.
Product grids are where a campaign turns into something people can buy. I set up the grid and its filters so the collection loaded with the right products and every tile resolved to a working product page.

gallery.title: Nike Soccer x LEGO Collection Shop
gallery.desc:
A Nike x LEGO Collection shop in the app, led by a Nike Soccer x LEGO Collection hero of minifigures in kit, with tabs for Shoes, Tops and T-Shirts and Hoodies above a product grid of LEGO sneaker builds.
I assembled the hero, the category tabs and the grid into one surface and checked that each tab filtered to the right products before it went live.

gallery.title: Men's Shop Tab with Category Navigation
gallery.desc:
The Men's view of the app's Shop tab, with a featured carousel opening on the Nike 24.7 Collection above category tiles for Shoes, Clothing, Accessories, Sport, Back to School and Sale.
This is the kind of full shopping surface I assembled one component at a time. Each tile carries its own imagery and menu routing, and the surface only works once every piece lands in the right place.

gallery.title: Sport Category Page in the Nike App
gallery.desc:
The Sport category page reached from the Shop tab, with a tennis hero, a featured row including Basketball Must-Haves and the ACG Chamo Camo Collection, and a menu running from All Conditions Gear through Golf.
Each row and menu item had its own routing into the parent surface. I built and checked them in sequence so no entry point led to an empty page.

gallery.title: Jannik Sinner Graphic Tee Product Page
gallery.desc:
A product page on Nike.com for the Jannik Sinner Men's NikeCourt Dri-FIT Graphic Tennis T-Shirt, with an image gallery, size selector, Add to Bag and pickup options.
This is where every placement and grid eventually has to land. A tile that routes anywhere else is a product someone cannot buy, so I traced destinations through to pages like this one before anything was scheduled.

gallery.title: Women's Back to School Bags Shop
gallery.desc:
A Women's Back to School Bags shop in the app, with tabs for Backpacks, Duffels and Drawstring Bags, a Back to School feature card promising top picks for staying ahead of the game, and a grid led by the Nike Varsity Elite.
I assembled the tabs, feature card and grid into one surface and checked each piece on device so every tab and tile resolved to the right products.

title: Christian's Work Portfolio with QAD Redzone

hero.title: Humanizing the Brand with Frontline Workers and Growing LinkedIn Engagement 550%
hero.subtitle: Integrated Creative for QAD Redzone

lede: Plants around the world run their frontline teams on QAD Redzone, a connected workforce platform whose tools deliver real-time productivity and compliance insight. The brand had room to grow past product features. Over three years I scaled Redzone's creative presence across web, video, print, and social, half of it facing customers and half facing the company's own people, and built all of it around the workers running the software.

blocks.h: THE PROBLEM
p: Manufacturing software tends to look as cold as the factory floor it serves, heavy on dashboards and distant from the people using it.

Redzone had a different story available. The results were there and so was the community impact, but the visual language had not caught up to either. The brand needed storytelling that put frontline workers on screen and a system that held together from one channel to the next.

blocks.h: THE SOLUTION
p: Leading with the people who used the software rebuilt how Redzone communicated. Campaign branding, social graphics, product explainers, physical activations, and original photography gave the frontline community a design system where they were the hero, and stat-driven banners and product overviews were held to the same standard: personal in tone, true to the energy on the floor.
LinkedIn engagement grew 550% (2% to 14%). Reels and YouTube reach tripled (20K to 60K).

Two hundred new web and intranet pages lifted traffic 33%, six-figure paid budgets turned into 1M+ ad interactions at twice the industry-average CTR, and lead generation rose 105% year over year, the work behind the 2024 Team Collaborator Award.

blocks.h: Simplifying Complex Features with Clean, On-Brand Visuals
p: Redzone's software is packed with capability, and none of it lands when it sits behind technical language and cluttered design. Competitors led with dense dashboards and cold UI screenshots that alienated more than they educated.

Starting with the tools manufacturing teams touched daily, I rebuilt how we explained them visually, so the work held up for existing users and for people meeting Redzone for the first time on our website or social channels. Branded feature graphics and light-motion assets blended interface mockups with messaging, and they lived in sales decks, on the website, in internal training, and across social.

The launch campaign for the Learning feature in the Redzone app on iPad and Apple TV grew out of this work. Workers on the plant floor were filmed using it to document repairs, and that footage became the selling point.

gallery.title: Productivity and Engagement with Manufacturing All Stars
gallery.desc:
Web banners I created highlighting productivity uplift and engagement stats while showing a real manufacturing team in their work environment. The goal was to ground the stat in something tangible — so instead of a cold chart, I layered the text over real candid photos of our customers that communicates trust, collaboration, and momentum.
The layout was optimized for use across paid media and retargeting campaigns. Clear, bold type and a focused stat allowed the message to cut through quickly, even in scroll-heavy environments.

gallery.src: QAD Redzone Presents_ Gary the GOAT
gallery.title: Parts Inventory Feature GIF with Gary
gallery.desc:
Inventory tracking isn’t always the most exciting topic — so I injected a little energy with a looping animation featuring our official mascot, Gary the Goat. This asset was used across social and product channels to spotlight Redzone’s inventory feature in a fun, digestible way.
The animation leads with visual clarity and ends with a wink. I designed it to feel native to the brand and built entirely in-house, allowing us to repurpose it in everything from web explainers to internal campaigns.

gallery.title: Redzone Resource Library and Video Pages
gallery.desc:
Real screenshots of the Redzone website at the time, showing two sides of it: a filterable resource library on desktop and a video page on mobile. Each card leads with a branded cover, from infographics like 'Analytics for Everyone' to the 'Tales of Triumph from the Factory Floor' ebook.
The goal was the same as the rest of my feature work: keep complex topics clean and inviting. On the video page, real team members fill the frame before the copy explains anything, so visitors meet the people first and the platform second.

blocks.h: Pushing Brand Voice and Visuals Through Creative Holiday Content
p: Holidays are filler for most software companies: a branded stock image with a timestamp. Seasonal moments were a chance to show that Redzone's voice could sound like the community the platform serves.

I led creative direction, scripting, design, and rollout across the holiday calendar, including New Year's reflections and April Fools' jokes. Tone shifted from one campaign to the next, and each turned a date on the calendar into a reason to talk with our community. Those posts became some of our highest-performing work, on and off the shop floor.

gallery.title: Redzone Vision Pro: April Fools’ Campaign
gallery.desc:
A real, but parody product launch for April Fools’ Day, this graphic introduced the fictional 'Redzone Vision Pro' — a mixed-reality headset with features exaggerating real use circumstances and promotion of an AR Goat Companion. I created the illustration, wrote mock release notes, and designed accompanying visuals that mimicked Apple’s branding with a Redzone twist.
This concept was expanded into a full microsite and teaser video, and was widely shared internally and externally as a standout moment of brand playfulness and design range.

gallery.title: Gary the Goat: Task Complete
gallery.desc:
Gary the Goat, Redzone's official mascot, is back in a short animated clip built around the satisfying moment a task gets checked off. Like the rest of the seasonal and playful content, it trades a generic post for a bit of personality the community could recognize.
I kept it brief and loopable so it works as a quick social moment, letting Gary carry the brand voice while the message stays simple: the work got done.

gallery.title: Redzone New Year's Post
gallery.desc: This post ushered in the new year by spotlighting real Redzone customers and a key milestone they reached with the platform. Rather than opt for a generic “Happy New Year” message, I focused the creative on human accomplishment — using candid and posed photography and a bold layout to reflect energy and optimism.

blocks.h: Building Culture, Community, and Educational Content Through Everyday Design
p: Social media at Redzone was a place to celebrate people and share what they knew, and the content direction covered playful culture posts and education-driven infographics, aimed at internal teams and the wider frontline community alike.

The employee anniversary series ran as stylized monthly calendars with illustrations for the time of year, each one a small spotlight on the people behind the company. Infographics and carousels translated topics like frontline retention and productivity gains into visuals people saved and shared.

Inside the company, the same instinct built the one-stop employee intranet that held onboarding, training, and policy material, the promotion behind WISE, our employee resource group for women and allies, and the school volunteer days, GivingTuesday drives, and community cleanups that got people to sign up.

gallery.title: The History of the Assembly Line
gallery.desc: This editorial-style series was created to support a feature on the Redzone blog and drive engagement on social channels. The design blends collage and texture-rich visuals to evoke different eras of manufacturing — starting with Henry Ford’s moving assembly line and ending in today’s AI-enhanced Industry 4.0. I developed a visual theme inspired by vintage magazines to make the information both nostalgic and futuristic, bridging the past and future of factory innovation through storytelling-led design.

gallery.title: Monthly Work Anniversary Calendars
gallery.desc: Each month, I designed custom-branded posts to celebrate Redzone employee anniversaries in a visually engaging way. These weren’t just internal shoutouts — they were small but powerful morale boosters that reminded teams they were valued. Each layout matched a seasonal theme, from heartfelt Valentine’s vibes to festive fireworks, with vibrant Redzone branding woven throughout. These graphics were shared company-wide and often sparked fun conversations and resharing among team members.

gallery.title: OEE Education Carousel
gallery.desc: I designed this carousel to break down one of Redzone’s more technical subjects: Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE). Each frame introduced an important subtopic — like minimizing downtime or identifying inefficiencies—while keeping the visuals clean, modern, and true to brand. I used illustrations to visualize the production line and custom iconography to add clarity to the stats-heavy content. This series was created for LinkedIn to support Redzone’s learning and compliance messaging in a more accessible and engaging way.

blocks.h: Extending the Brand into the Real World with Physical Touchpoints
p: Branded experiences people could see, wear, hold, and remember pushed the creative into physical space. A creatively packaged iPad sent to a prospective customer. A jumbotron activation on the expo floor.
Each piece was made to feel human, start a conversation, and strengthen Redzone's presence in a form you could pick up and pass around.

gallery.title: Redzone Factory Floor Shirt & Logo Design
gallery.desc: For this piece of custom swag, I created an original character inspired by early animation styles — think Steamboat Willie, but on the factory floor. The design featured a personified iPad with gloved hands and sneakers. It was a lighthearted way to visualize Redzone’s connected workforce in motion, blending nostalgia with modern tech. This piece became a favorite among team members for its style — and for capturing how even software can have personality.

gallery.title: Jumbotron Video Loop for Trade Show Booth
gallery.desc: For a major trade show with a football stadium theme, I collaborated with the events team to ideate a large-scale video loop tailored for the jumbotron at our booth. The creative needed to be bold, high-contrast, and movement-rich — designed to be eye-catching from across the venue. I helped incorporate footage from multiple campaigns, layered animated UI previews, and added messaging that aligned with the game-day energy of the environment.

gallery.title: Slide-to-Unlock iPad Mailer for Prospective Customers
gallery.desc:
To break through the noise of traditional sales mailers, I designed an interactive iPad box experience that played on the nostalgic 'slide to unlock' gesture from early tablets and phones. The exterior featured a sleek cutout window with a movable paper insert. When slid from side to side, phrases like 'Empowering the Frontline' and 'Unlock Your Factory’s Potential' were revealed — turning the unboxing into a small moment of delight.
The design balanced polish with surprise, all while supporting a sales strategy that put product value and people front and center.
The mailer was distributed to select prospects based on their stage in the sales funnel, generating curiosity, conversation, and conversions.

gallery.title: LinkedIn Photo Activation: Tag to Win
gallery.desc: To drive social engagement at our trade shows, I designed a physical LinkedIn post cutout for attendees to pose with. The frame mimicked the layout of a real LinkedIn post and included branded prompts to tag Redzone. The activation worked as both a selfie opportunity and a conversation starter — leading to dozens of shares and direct traffic from new prospects on social.

blocks.h: Amplifying Culture & Capability Through Video
p: Video made the product more approachable, the features more digestible, and the people behind the software more visible. I concepted, scripted, directed, and edited work ranging from step-by-step walkthroughs to the story of Women Inspiring Success and Empowerment (WISE).

The rule was the same each time: team members speaking directly to camera, laughter left in the edit, visuals that said our tech exists to serve real people doing real work. These videos ran across internal communications, social launches, and onboarding.

gallery.title: A Closer Look into QAD Redzone's 4 Modules
gallery.desc:
A four-minute overview of Redzone's four connected modules (Productivity, Compliance, Reliability, and Learning) and how they work together on the factory floor. I concepted, scripted, directed, and edited it as the starting point for anyone new to Redzone or weighing the full platform.
Instead of a screen-recorded feature list, team members walk through the platform on camera, so the software reads as something real people use to communicate faster and fix problems sooner.

gallery.title: Women Inspiring Success and Empowerment (WISE): Women's History Month 2025
gallery.desc:
A Women's History Month piece telling the story of Women Inspiring Success and Empowerment (WISE) through team members speaking directly to camera, in their own words and with the laughter left in.
It ran across internal communications and social, putting the people behind the software at the center instead of the product.

gallery.title: Deep Dive into QAD Redzone Modules
gallery.desc:
The longer walkthrough, built around the 29% productivity increase behind the platform. It shows each module in action, from live OEE, throughput, and downtime data in Productivity to a fully paperless shop floor in Compliance, with production, quality, and maintenance teams working from the same live data.
Where the overview earns attention, this one answers the detailed questions prospects and new users bring next.

gallery.title: Women Inspiring Success and Empowerment (WISE): International Women's Day 2024
gallery.desc:
The International Women's Day piece that set the format for WISE the year before: real team members, unscripted moments, and an edit that feels like a conversation rather than a corporate announcement.
Shared across internal communications and social, it helped make WISE visible across the company and beyond it.

blocks.h: Supporting Visual Consistency Through Custom Brand Photography
p: When the moment called for it, I captured original photography for social and web, focused on people, process, and production. These images ran across campaign launches, blog posts, and internal assets and kept the brand's tone consistent with the push toward a more human identity.

gallery.title: Candid Conversation on the Expo Floor
gallery.desc:
A Redzone team member laughs mid-conversation with two attendees in red shirts on a busy trade show floor. Moments like this are what I looked for at events: real reactions, not staged handshakes.
Shots like this fed social posts and event recaps, giving the brand's human-first direction an unposed face.

gallery.title: Tee Shot at a Redzone Golf Outing
gallery.desc:
Shot from behind the gallery, this frame catches a golfer just after impact, with two onlookers framing the drive against an open Texas-blue sky. I liked the layered depth, which puts the viewer in the group watching.
Community events were part of the Redzone story too, and photos like this showed the relationships behind the software away from the plant floor.

gallery.title: Celebrating a Paperless Shop Floor
gallery.desc:
Plant workers in hard hats and lab coats throw sheets of paper into the air, a spontaneous celebration of going paperless. It is the kind of moment no stock library can supply.
I kept the frame loose and energetic so the joy reads first. The image puts frontline workers at the center of the story Redzone tells about its compliance tools.

gallery.title: Evening Reception Under Warm Lantern Light
gallery.desc:
A packed reception fills a dramatic venue lit by amber lanterns, with a towering multi-armed statue as the backdrop. I shot from above to capture the scale of the crowd and the glow of the room together.
Event photography like this showed how much of the Redzone community gathered in person, giving campaign and recap posts a sense of place.

gallery.title: Students on a Food Production Floor Tour
gallery.desc:
In hairnets, gowns and blue gloves, a group of young visitors listens closely as a plant team member walks them through the production line. The shot centers on their attention, not the equipment.
I captured it to show the community side of manufacturing: plants opening their doors to the next generation of frontline workers.

gallery.title: Morning at The Hills Course
gallery.desc:
Golf bags in the foreground lead the eye past a stone marker for The Hills Course, a clubhouse clock, and carts heading out. It is a quiet establishing shot that sets the scene before the play begins.
I used frames like this to give event coverage a sense of place, so the recap felt like a day out with the community and not a run of headshots.

gallery.title: Productivity Roadshow Stop with an IndyCar
gallery.desc:
A Redzone 'Productivity NOW for Manufacturing' banner stands beside a full IndyCar and racing suit on a checkered floor while guests mingle. The setting brings real energy to a software event.
I framed the car and the conversation together so the photo works both as an event recap and as proof that the community showed up in person.

gallery.title: Redzone Community Awards 2024 Main Stage
gallery.desc:
The main screen announces the 10th Anniversary Redzone Community Awards 2024 over fireworks graphics, with a row of numbered Redzone jerseys lit up below. The crowd in silhouette keeps the focus on the stage.
I captured the room as the event opened, giving the community recap an establishing shot that conveys the scale and celebration of the night.

gallery.title: Live Painting of the Golf Course
gallery.desc:
Over an artist's shoulder, a canvas of the golf course takes shape, with figures, flag and fairway painted in real time while the actual green stretches out beyond. The over-the-shoulder angle puts the viewer right at the easel.
I liked how it captured a slower, creative moment inside a busy event day, adding warmth and variety to the coverage.

title: Christian's Work Portfolio with SOLV Energy

hero.title: How I Modernized SOLV Energy's Web Presence and Built Power Apps That Streamlined Internal Workflows
hero.subtitle: Internal Tools & External Web for SOLV Energy

lede: SOLV Energy is a lifecycle partner for utility-scale solar, storage, and energy infrastructure across the United States. With more than 20 GW of solar and storage under management and a fast-growing public profile (Nasdaq: MWH), SOLV Energy needed a digital presence that could keep pace with a company building, operating, and announcing at industry scale. This case study covers how I supported and built that digital presence across web, internal tools, graphic design, and video.

blocks.h: THE PROBLEM
p: A renewable energy company has a harder communications job than most. SOLV Energy's audiences include investors, customers, prospective hires, craft workers, community partners, and thousands of employees in offices and on jobsites across the country. Each audience needs different proof points, different formats, and different channels. Communications systems had not kept pace with that growth. The SOLV Energy website needed steady, accurate updates as new projects, leadership news, and milestones landed. Internal teams needed faster, lighter ways to share approved content to their own networks. Visual storytelling needed to keep up with a project pipeline running nationally and in dozens of states at once.

blocks.h: THE SOLUTION
p: I built a digital backbone that handled the day-to-day weight: a continuously updated external website, internal tools that turned approved content into employee-shareable assets, graphic design at the cadence project announcements demanded, and video work that brought the work on the ground into focus. Each piece was designed to scale with the company rather than break under it.

blocks.h: Owning the Web Presence and Internal Tooling of a Public Energy Infrastructure Company
p: A public company moves fast, and its website has to move with it. I maintained and continuously updated solvenergy.com through WordPress, publishing project announcements, leadership additions, earnings news, and partnership wins as they landed. Updates often went live within hours of internal approval, with formatting, imagery, and SEO considerations dialed in before publish.

Beyond the external site, I built and launched an Employee Advocacy platform powered by Power Apps. Built to give SOLV Energy teammates one place to find pre-approved social content to share with their own networks, the platform turned a manual, email-based workflow into a self-serve experience. Employees can browse, preview, and share posts directly to their LinkedIn in seconds.
Together, those efforts kept the company's external presence current while activating the internal community as a force multiplier for visibility, advocacy, and recruiting.

gallery.title: SOLV Energy Homepage Hero Walkthrough
gallery.desc:
This is the front door of solvenergy.com: a wide aerial of a solar field, the SOLV mark, and a hero line that sums up the company in four words, Powering Progress with Proven Execution. I kept the site current as project, leadership, and earnings news landed.
Updates often went live within hours of internal approval, with formatting, imagery, and SEO handled before publish so the homepage always reflected where the company actually was.

gallery.title: Employee Advocacy Power App in Action
gallery.desc:
Sharing approved content used to mean digging through emails. I built this Employee Advocacy platform in Power Apps so SOLV Energy teammates have one place to find pre-approved posts, sorted by tags like Impact, Mission, and Project Spotlight.
Each card previews the post before sharing, and employees can push it straight to their LinkedIn in seconds. The result turned a manual workflow into a self-serve experience that helps with visibility and recruiting.

gallery.title: Publishing a News Article Behind the Scenes
gallery.desc:
Here's a look at the publishing side of the job: an article entry with its title, one-sentence extract, background image, and subject and media categories, shown next to a live preview of the SOLV Energy news page.
Every announcement went through this kind of setup before going live. I checked formatting, imagery, and categorization in the preview so each story looked right the moment it published.

gallery.title: Design, Build, Operate, Optimize Services Page
gallery.desc:
A scroll through one of solvenergy.com's interior pages, opening on crews in hard hats at work in the field and the headline Design. Build. Operate. Optimize. It explains SOLV Energy's end-to-end services for solar, battery storage, and high-voltage infrastructure.
I kept pages like this accurate and current as the company grew, so customers and investors landing deeper in the site found the same polish as the homepage.

blocks.h: Designing at the Speed of a Public Company's News Cycle
p: When SOLV Energy goes public, breaks ground, or sends an executive to a conference, the visuals supporting that moment have to be ready as soon as possible and sometimes on the same day. I produced ongoing graphic design across speaker session cards, kudos and recognition posts, project announcements, and case study teasers, working within and gradually extending SOLV Energy's visual system.

Design prioritized clean composition, brand-consistent color palettes anchored on SOLV Energy's signature colors, and a headline hierarchy that made each graphic legible at thumbnail scale on social feeds. Every asset shipped quickly without sacrificing the polish an investor-grade or customer-facing audience expects.

gallery.title: RE+ 2025 Event and Speaking Session Graphics
gallery.desc:
For RE+ in Las Vegas, I made a pair of graphics: a bold blue announcement for the event and a darker companion piece listing SOLV Energy's two speaking sessions with Eric Butticaz, Director of Apprenticeship, including times and rooms.
The Venetian skyline and SOLV's sunburst mark tie the two together, while the lime accents and clear type keep the session details easy to read at thumbnail size on social.

gallery.title: Conference Speaker Card and Kudos Post
gallery.desc:
These two cover both sides of SOLV Energy's event presence. On the left, a speaking session card for CFO Chad Plotkin at the 38th Annual ROTH Conference. On the right, a kudos post recognizing Kate for representing the company at the 2026 IECA Annual Conference & Expo.
Both are built on the brand's signature blues and sunburst motif, with a headline hierarchy that stays readable even as a small social thumbnail.

gallery.title: Announcement and Case Study Teaser Graphics
gallery.desc:
Not every post needs a face. The left graphic is an "In Case You Missed It" announcement about SOLV Energy's O&M scale and largest single-site agreement, set over a field photo of solar panels and wildflowers.
The right is a case study teaser that opens with a question about underperforming sites. I let the white space and the sunburst frame do the work, ending with a simple prompt to read the case study.

blocks.h: Bringing Field Stories and Project Milestones to Life Through Video
p: Video is how SOLV Energy makes its work tangible to audiences who will never visit a jobsite. I helped concept, script, and produce multiple social media videos and internal content for project milestones, customer testimonials, and culture moments, with a focus on letting the people doing the work speak for themselves.
Editing stayed minimal and the people stayed central, with on-site capture, light branding overlay, and pacing tuned for both LinkedIn and longer-form internal use.

gallery.title: Good Energy
gallery.desc:
A vertical social video that opens on a sweeping aerial of a SOLV Energy project under construction, with crews, trucks, and structures spread across the site. It's part of the short-form work I helped concept, script, and produce for project milestones and culture moments.
Editing stayed minimal so the work on the ground carried the story, with light branding and pacing tuned for social feeds.

gallery.title: A Message from SOLV Energy CEO, George Hershman
gallery.desc:
Sometimes the best move is to let leadership talk. In this piece, CEO George Hershman speaks directly to camera in a relaxed interview setting about SOLV Energy and its work.
I kept the edit simple and the speaker central, matching the approach I used across SOLV's video content: let the people behind the company speak for themselves, with branding that supports the message instead of competing with it.

gallery.title: Overview and Impact of Misae Solar
gallery.desc:
This vertical video gives a site overview of the Misae Solar project, starting with a drone shot over rows of panels stretching toward the horizon. It was one of several pieces I helped produce to show audiences what SOLV Energy's projects look like up close.
I paired on-site footage with light brand overlays and kept the pacing quick enough for LinkedIn while still giving the scale of the site room to land.

gallery.title: We Power What's Next at SOLV Energy
gallery.desc:
This one opens somewhere unexpected for an energy company: a deep blue night sky full of stars. From there, it builds toward SOLV Energy's line, We Power What's Next, as a culture piece for both social and internal audiences.
I helped concept and produce it with the same rule I used across SOLV's video work: minimal editing, the people kept central, and pacing that fits LinkedIn and longer-form internal use alike.

title: Christian's Work Portfolio with Cohesity

hero.title: How I Led 3,000 Employee Advocacy and Cross-Channel Design at Cohesity
hero.subtitle: Employee Advocacy and Integrated Creative for an AI-Powered Data Security Leader

lede: Cohesity is the leader in AI-powered data security and management, trusted by 70% of the Global 500 across 140+ countries. While the company protects the world's most critical data, its brand and content needed to feel as human as the people behind it. This case study explores how I helped power Cohesity's Champions employee advocacy program and design cohesive creative across PR, blogs, newsletters, and global events.

blocks.h: THE PROBLEM
p: Enterprise cybersecurity content has a reputation. It's dense, technical, and written for boardrooms instead of the people who actually share it, read it, and live with the threats it covers. Cohesity had powerful product news, deep customer stories, and real industry credibility, but the social voice and visual presence often felt indistinguishable from the rest of the enterprise software space. Employees weren't sharing content they didn't connect with, and the brand was missing chances to land with both internal advocates and external audiences in a way that felt human, modern, and worth talking about.

blocks.h: THE SOLUTION
p: I rebuilt how Cohesity showed up. I authored a new brand voice for the Champions employee advocacy program, closer to Duolingo and Figma social than corporate LinkedIn, and operationalized a daily content engine that fed 3,000+ active Champions with posts they actually wanted to share. Alongside the advocacy work, I led original creative design across PR campaigns, blog hero graphics, newsletter design, and global event activations. The result was a Cohesity presence that felt sharper, faster, and more share-worthy across every customer-facing channel.

blocks.h: Reframing Cohesity's Voice for an Employee Advocacy Program That Actually Got Shared
p: I rebuilt Cohesity's Employee Advocacy program from the ground up, authoring a new brand voice closer to Duolingo and Figma social than corporate LinkedIn and running a daily content engine for 3,000+ advocates globally. Beyond core post writing, I led the redesign of the program, internal competitions, expanded program reach into international markets, connected advocacy work across multiple departments, and headed an executive advocacy program where I personally wrote and edited posts for the Chief Product and Chief Financial Officers. The result was a sharper, faster Cohesity voice that turned employee voices into one of the company's strongest social channels.

gallery.title: Champions Advocacy Hub Trending Posts Feed
gallery.desc:
This is where Cohesity's Champions found content to share each day. The Trending Posts view shows the week's most active posts, from the HPE alliance to the agentic support portal, with a live feed of colleagues sharing alongside.
I wrote the posts that filled this feed in a voice closer to Duolingo and Figma social than corporate LinkedIn, so 3,000+ advocates actually wanted to post them. Leaderboards and challenges kept the energy up.

gallery.title: The Empire Strikes Backups Champions Newsletter
gallery.desc:
A Star Wars nod for a data security company was too good to pass up. The Empire Strikes Backups newsletter opens with a glowing green title over a starfield, followed by a Top Content to Share ticker and story cards with one-click Share buttons.
I designed it to make sharing feel like a game for Champions, pulling the week's best posts into a single scroll so advocates could share in seconds without hunting for links.

blocks.h: Pushing Brand Voice and Visuals Through Creative Holiday Content
p: Beyond employee advocacy, I supported the creative team across Cohesity's most visible moments, including partnership campaigns with Google Cloud, AWS, NVIDIA, Hewlett-Packard, and Microsoft, blog hero graphics for executive thought leadership, weekly Security Spotlight and Empire Strikes Backups newsletter creative, and event activations. The visual language had to feel modern enough to compete with consumer-grade design while still landing credibility in enterprise cybersecurity.

gallery.title: Webinar, Hiring, and NVIDIA GTC Social Graphics
gallery.desc:
Three posts, three different jobs: a webinar promo on ransomware gang behavior, a bold pink We're Hiring card for a role in São Paulo, and an event graphic for Cohesity at NVIDIA GTC 2026.
Each one leans on Cohesity's green and magenta palette and tight condensed type, so they read like a set while handling very different messages. The goal was consumer-grade energy that still felt credible in enterprise security.

gallery.title: Google Cloud Next, Blog Hero, and Newsletter Creative
gallery.desc:
A mix from Cohesity's busiest channels: a booth promo for Google Cloud Next 26 in Las Vegas, a blog hero announcing that the future of support is here and it's agentic, and a punchy Your backups are next. graphic.
I kept each piece simple and direct, letting the bright green and big type carry the message so it held up across events, blogs, and weekly Security Spotlight newsletter creative.
